result:
I graded submission s2 for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. You got 3 correct, 2 partial and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | An agent is defined by the loop, not by a longer prompt or a bigger model. |
| q2 | correct | The model only outputs a tool request; the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | wrong | You chose "it will eventually fix the bug", which is misconception M6. The agent gets the same failing result every step, so more steps add nothing. It needs a stopping condition such as a step limit. Extra steps also cost model usage. |
| q4 | partial | 4 is the right count. But you wrote that the model "runs" each tool itself, which is misconception M4. The model only requests a tool, and the program runs it. |
| q5 | correct | You gave both parts: the result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to decide what to do next. |
| q6 | partial | The name is part of how the model chooses. It relies on the whole description: the name, what the tool does and its parameters. |

You have the core loop down. The model only requests tools and never runs them, and every loop needs a stopping condition.

Next step: rewrite `check_calendar`'s description so the model could pick it without seeing any code. Then re-read the part of the agent-loop lesson on stopping conditions.

I also added a learning record (`learning-records/0003-quiz-0001-second-attempt.md`) and updated `NOTES.md`. `submissions/s1.json` is still ungraded.
